newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PSE CONSIDERS NEW MARKET FOR SMALL ISSUES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PSE CONSIDERS NEW MARKET FOR SMALL ISSUES.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange is considering the creation of a new market to trade equities in smaller companies, PSE Chairman Tomas Jezek told a news conference on Wednesday.
"We want to, in a year, put onto the bourse a new market intended for small and medium companies to cultivate the culture of the capital market," Jezek said.
The PSE has delisted about 500 issues with low liquidity from trading on the bourse's free market with another 500 expected to be removed from trading by the end of May.

Ultimately the bourse wants to have only a few hundred stocks -- out of the more than 1,700 issues introduced through the country's massive voucher privatisation programme earlier in the decade -- trading on its three markets.
The new bourse for smaller issues would take the place of the so-called "free" market where most of the thinly traded stocks being removed are currently listed.
Most of the PSE's turnover is concentrated on the 45-share main market, which has stricter listing requirements, or on the parallel market with less-rigid standards.
